_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for CRM retrospectives (retro/build_crm.py), generated from salesforce.com's own filings: every raw figure is the row string it appears in (kept in 'rows'), checked against its filing, and every growth rate, margin and rule-T value is computed from those figures. Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date (EDGAR's acceptance time in ET; after the 16:00 close, the next trading day).

listing.quote: Our common stock has been quoted on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol “CRM” since June 23, 2004.

fiscal_calendar.quote: Our fiscal year ends on January 31.

price_basis: Yahoo's CRM series is adjusted for the four-for-one split of 2013-04-18; the builder multiplies it by the splits after AS_OF (x4 in 2008-2009), so every price is the price as traded

history_vintages.why: 'We are the leading provider, based on market share, of application services that allow organizations to easily share customer information on demand, according to a December 2006 report by International Data Corporation, or IDC.' 'The market for CRM applications is intensely competitive and rapidly changing, barriers to entry are relatively low, several of our competitors are larger and have more resources than we do, and with the introduction of new technologies and market entrants, we expect competition to intensify in the future.' 'enterprise software application vendors including Amdocs Limited, Infor Global Solutions, Epicor, IBM Corporation, Microsoft Corporation, SAP AG, and Oracle Corporation;' (FY2007 10-K); DURABLE: no 10-K calls the business cyclical ('cycle' appears only as the sales cycle and payment cycles)

eps_excluded.2007: FY2007 is excluded: GAAP diluted EPS $0.00 ('For the full year, GAAP earnings per share were breakeven', the Q4 FY07 release; net income $481K), so the year has no P/E (the F rule for Ford's $0.00 year), and no item in it is listed as a one-off

eps_first_excluded.2004: excluded, a year distorted by a one-off benefit (the AVGO FY2018 mirror test): its $3,445K lease recovery ('Lease recovery' in the selected data) is larger than the year's $794K of pre-tax income without it (pre-tax $4,239K), so the reported $0.04 is more than double the year's EPS without it, and no filing publishes a figure excluding it; an excluded year that is not the latest takes the years before it (the PFE 2003 and MU FY2003 rule; the inception period to January 2000 and fiscal 2001-2003 are losses as well: $(0.55), $(2.38), $(1.36), $(0.37)), so the history and the P/E window start after January 31, 2004, and the window from the listing on 2004-06-23

history_vintages.normalization: GAAP diluted EPS, each year from the latest filing that reports it (FY2007 10-K for fiscal 2005-2007), except FY06 at the company's $0.181 excluding only the reversal of the deferred tax valuation allowance and the lease recovery (Q4 FY06 release; GAAP $0.24: the ACN rule, the JPM FY2017 rule for a figure only the release prints); the releases of Q4 FY07 on print GAAP only; FY2007 is excluded: GAAP diluted EPS $0.00 ('For the full year, GAAP earnings per share were breakeven', the Q4 FY07 release; net income $481K), so the year has no P/E (the F rule for Ford's $0.00 year), and no item in it is listed as a one-off; it is the latest year in the FY2007 10-K, so only its own days leave the P/E window, and it stays a gap after (the NKE FY2018 and XOM FY2020 rule)

rule_t._doc: Rule T over fiscal 1998-2007, the decade of the FY2007 10-K (the vintage public on 2008-01-04): salesforce.com's first period runs from its inception (February 3, 1999) to January 31, 2000 and has no revenue ('Total revenues | — | 5,435 | ...', the prospectus), so the changes are fiscal 2002-2007, each from the latest filing published by 2008-01-04 that reports both years (the FY2005 10-K for fiscal 2001-2002, the FY2006 10-K for 2002-2003, the FY2007 10-K for 2003-2007); deferred revenue has five (no filing reports the January 31, 2001 balance)
